title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Cases of Objection and Reconsideration in Enforcement by People's Courts

articles.content_en:
Article 2: Where an enforcement objection meets the conditions provided in Article 225 or Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall docket the case within three days and, within three days after docketing, notify the objector and the relevant parties. If the acceptance conditions are not met, it shall rule not to accept the case; if after docketing it is discovered that the acceptance conditions are not met, it shall rule to dismiss the application.
If the materials for an enforcement objection are incomplete, the People's Court shall inform the objector at one time to supplement them within three days; if they are not supplemented within the prescribed period, the objection shall not be accepted.
If the objector is dissatisfied with the ruling on non-acceptance or dismissal of the application, the objector may apply to the People's Court at the next higher level for reconsideration within ten days from the date of service of the ruling. After review, if the higher People's Court considers that the acceptance conditions are met, it shall rule to revoke the original ruling and instruct the executing court to docket the case or to review the enforcement objection.

Article 3: Where the executing court, within three days after receiving an enforcement objection, neither dockets the case nor makes a ruling of non-acceptance, or after accepting the case, fails to make a ruling on the objection beyond the statutory period without justifiable reasons, the objector may raise an objection to the People's Court at the next higher level. If the higher People's Court, after review, considers that the reasons are established, it shall instruct the executing court to docket the case within three days or to make a ruling on the objection within fifteen days.

Article 4: After an enforcement case is designated for enforcement by another court, escalated to a higher-level court for enforcement, or entrusted for enforcement, if a party or interested party raises an objection to the enforcement acts of the original executing court, the case shall be reviewed and handled by the People's Court responsible for enforcing the case at the time the objection is raised; if the designated or entrusted People's Court is a lower-level court relative to the original executing court, the original executing court shall still conduct the review and handling.
After an enforcement case is designated for enforcement, escalated to a higher-level court for enforcement, or entrusted for enforcement, if a person not involved in the case raises an objection to the subject matter of enforcement under the original executing court, the preceding paragraph shall be applied by reference.

Article 6: Where a party or interested party raises an objection pursuant to Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law, the objection shall be raised before the conclusion of the enforcement procedure, except for an objection to a measure concluding enforcement.
Where a person not involved in the case raises an objection pursuant to Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law, the objection shall be raised before the conclusion of enforcement of the subject matter of enforcement to which the objection is directed; if the subject matter of enforcement is transferred to a party, the objection shall be raised before the conclusion of the enforcement procedure.

Article 8: Where a person not involved in the case, based on substantive rights, both raises an objection to exclude enforcement against the subject matter of enforcement and, as an interested party, raises an objection to an enforcement act, the People's Court shall review the case pursuant to Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law.
Where a person not involved in the case, based on substantive rights, raises an objection to exclude enforcement against the subject matter of enforcement and, at the same time, as an interested party, raises an objection to an enforcement act unrelated to substantive rights, the People's Court shall review the case separately pursuant to Article 227 and Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 9: Where a person whose departure from the country is restricted considers that the restriction on departure is erroneous, the person may apply to the People's Court at the next higher level for reconsideration within ten days from the date of receipt of the decision restricting departure. The higher People's Court shall make a decision within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the reconsideration application. During the reconsideration period, the execution of the original decision shall not be suspended.

Article 10: Where a party is dissatisfied with a ruling dismissing an application for non-enforcement of a notarized debt instrument, the party may apply to the People's Court at the next higher level for reconsideration within ten days from the date of receipt of the ruling. The higher People's Court shall review the application within thirty days from the date of receipt of the reconsideration application; if the reasons are established, it shall rule to revoke the original ruling and refuse to enforce the notarized debt instrument; if the reasons are not established, it shall rule to dismiss the reconsideration application. During the reconsideration period, enforcement shall not be suspended.

Article 11: When the People's Court reviews an enforcement objection or reconsideration case, it shall form a collegial panel according to law.
For an enforcement objection case ordered to be reviewed anew, a different collegial panel shall be formed.
Personnel handling enforcement implementation cases shall not participate in the review of the relevant enforcement objection and reconsideration cases.

Article 12: The People's Court shall conduct a written review of enforcement objection and reconsideration cases. Where the facts of the case are complex or the disputes are significant, a hearing shall be held.

Article 13: During the review period of an enforcement objection or reconsideration case, where the objector or the applicant for reconsideration applies to withdraw the objection or reconsideration application, whether to permit the withdrawal shall be ruled by the People's Court.

Article 14: Where an objector or applicant for reconsideration, after being lawfully summoned, refuses to attend a hearing without justifiable reasons, or withdraws from the hearing midway without permission from the court, thereby making it impossible for the People's Court to ascertain the relevant facts, the objector or applicant shall bear the adverse consequences on its own.

Article 15: Where a party or interested party has multiple grounds for objection to the same enforcement act but fails to raise them all together during the review of the objection, and after withdrawing the objection or being ruled to have the objection dismissed, raises an objection to the same enforcement act again, the People's Court shall not accept it.
Where a person not involved in the case, after withdrawing an objection or being ruled to have the objection dismissed, raises an objection to the same subject matter of enforcement again, the People's Court shall not accept it.

Article 16: When the People's Court makes a ruling pursuant to Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall inform the relevant right holder of the right and time limit for applying for reconsideration.
When the People's Court makes a ruling pursuant to Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law, it shall inform the relevant right holder of the right and time limit for bringing an action for objection to enforcement.
When the People's Court makes other rulings or decisions, if laws or judicial interpretations provide for the right and time limit of the relevant right holder to apply for reconsideration, the People's Court shall inform the right holder accordingly.

Article 18: During the enforcement process, where a third party is added as a party subject to enforcement because it made a written commitment to voluntarily repay the debt on behalf of the party subject to enforcement, and afterward repents without justifiable reasons and raises an objection, the People's Court shall not support the objection.

Article 19: Where the parties owe each other due debts, and the party subject to enforcement requests set-off, if the debt requested to be set off meets the following conditions, the People's Court shall support the request, unless set-off is prohibited by law or by the nature of the debt:
(1) the debt has been confirmed by a lawful instrument that has taken effect or has been recognized by the applicant for enforcement; and
(2) the subject matter of the debt is of the same kind and quality as the debt owed by the party subject to enforcement.

Article 20: In the enforcement of a monetary claim, if any of the following circumstances exists, and the party subject to enforcement raises an objection on the ground that the subject matter of enforcement is the residential house necessary for the subsistence of the party and its dependent family members, the People's Court shall not support the objection:
(1) a person who has a duty to support the party subject to enforcement has another residential house sufficient to maintain the necessities of life under his or her name;
(2) after the enforcement instrument takes effect, the party subject to enforcement transferred its other houses under its name to evade debts; or
(3) the applicant for enforcement provides a residential house for the party subject to enforcement and its dependent family members in accordance with the local standard for the guaranteed area of low-rent housing, or agrees to deduct five to eight years' rent from the proceeds of the sale of the house with reference to the average rental standard of the local housing rental market.
Where the enforcement instrument determines that the party subject to enforcement shall deliver a residential house, and a grace period of three months has already been given from the date of service of the enforcement notice, if the party subject to enforcement raises an objection on the ground that the house is a necessity for the subsistence of the party and its dependent family members, the People's Court shall not support the objection.

Article 22: Where a notarized debt instrument confers the force of compulsory execution on both the principal debt and the secured debt, the People's Court shall enforce it; where it confers the force of compulsory execution only on the principal debt and does not involve the secured debt, an application for enforcement of the secured debt shall not be accepted; where it confers the force of compulsory execution only on the secured debt and does not involve the principal debt, an application for enforcement of the principal debt shall not be accepted.
After the People's Court accepts an application for enforcement of a secured debt, if the party subject to enforcement applies for non-enforcement solely on the ground that the security contract does not fall within the scope of notarized debt instruments to which the force of compulsory execution is conferred, the application shall not be supported.

Article 24: With respect to an objection to exclude enforcement raised by a person not involved in the case, the People's Court shall review the following:
(1) whether the person not involved in the case is the right holder;
(2) the legality and authenticity of the right; and
(3) whether the right can exclude enforcement.

Article 26: In the enforcement of a monetary claim, where a person not involved in the case raises an objection to exclude enforcement based on a lawful instrument that has taken effect in another case and was made before the subject matter of enforcement was seized, attached, or frozen, the People's Court shall handle the matter according to the following circumstances:
(1) if the instrument is a judgment or ruling made in a dispute over ownership between the person not involved in the case and the party subject to enforcement, or in a contract dispute such as lease, borrowing, or custody that does not have the purpose of transferring the ownership of property, which determines or rules that the subject matter of enforcement belongs to the person not involved in the case or that it shall be returned to such person, and the right of such person can exclude enforcement, the objection shall be supported;
(2) if the instrument is a judgment or ruling made in a dispute over claims between the person not involved in the case and the party subject to enforcement other than the contracts listed in the preceding item, which determines or rules that the subject matter of enforcement belongs to the person not involved in the case or that it shall be delivered or returned to such person, the objection shall not be supported;
(3) if the instrument is a ruling on the conclusion of an auction or forced sale or a ruling on satisfaction of a debt by transfer of property under which the person not involved in the case acquires the subject matter of enforcement, and the right of such person can exclude enforcement, the objection shall be supported.
In the enforcement of a monetary claim, where a person not involved in the case raises an objection to exclude enforcement based on a lawful instrument that has taken effect in another case and was made after the subject matter of enforcement was seized, attached, or frozen, the People's Court shall not support the objection.
In the enforcement of a non-monetary claim, where a person not involved in the case raises an objection to exclude enforcement based on a lawful instrument that has taken effect in another case, and that instrument makes a different determination on the ownership of the subject matter of enforcement, the People's Court shall inform the person not involved in the case to apply for a retrial according to law or resolve the matter through other procedures.
Where the applicant for enforcement or the person not involved in the case is dissatisfied with a ruling made by the People's Court in accordance with the provisions in the first and second paragraphs of this Article, the applicant or person may bring an action for objection to enforcement pursuant to Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Article 27: Where the applicant for enforcement enjoys, according to law, a security interest or other priority right to satisfaction against the person not involved in the case with respect to the subject matter of enforcement, the People's Court shall not support the objection to exclude enforcement raised by the person not involved in the case, unless otherwise provided by laws or judicial interpretations.

Article 29: In the enforcement of a monetary claim, where a buyer raises an objection to commercial housing registered in the name of the real estate development enterprise subject to enforcement, and the following circumstances are met and the buyer's right can exclude enforcement, the People's Court shall support the objection:
(1) a lawful and valid written sales contract has been signed before the seizure by the People's Court;
(2) the purchased commercial housing is used for residence and the buyer has no other housing for residence under his or her name; and
(3) the price paid exceeds 50 percent of the total price stipulated in the contract.

Article 30: In the enforcement of a monetary claim, with respect to seized immovable property for which a notice registration of the transfer of real right has been made, if the transferee raises an objection to stop disposition, the People's Court shall support the objection; if the conditions for registration of the real right are met and the transferee raises an objection to exclude enforcement, the People's Court shall support the objection.

Article 31: Where a lessee requests to prevent the delivery of possession of the immovable property subject to enforcement to the transferee during the lease term, and a lawful and valid written lease contract has been signed and the lessee has taken possession and used the property before the seizure by the People's Court, the People's Court shall support the request.
Where the lessee and the party subject to enforcement maliciously collude to lease the immovable property subject to enforcement at an obviously unreasonable low price or forge evidence of rent payment, the People's Court shall not support the request to prevent delivery of possession.

Article 32: These Provisions shall apply to enforcement objection and reconsideration cases that have not been finally reviewed before these Provisions come into force. Where, for enforcement objection and reconsideration cases that have been finally reviewed before these Provisions come into force, the People's Court initiates an enforcement supervision procedure according to law, these Provisions shall not apply.
